title: The War Prayer
summary: "The War Prayer" is a short piece by Mark Twain, written late in his life and published posthumously. It opens in a church on the eve of a nation's departure to war, where patriotic fervour runs high and young volunteers, their families and the congregation are caught up in dreams of glory. A minister offers a long prayer asking God to grant victory and bless the country's soldiers. Then an aged, mysterious stranger appears, claiming to bring a message from the Throne. He explains that every prayer contains an unspoken part, and he reads out the hidden wish within the minister's plea: the death, suffering and ruin of the enemy's soldiers, families and children. The text is a sharp satire of wartime jingoism and of the comfortable religion that blesses violence in God's name. It is a short work, less a story than a moral argument delivered as a dramatic monologue.
